name: BIRAC - BIG
application_open: 1st January, 1st July
about: The Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG) scheme, initiated by BIRAC, supports early-stage biotech entrepreneurs and innovators in transforming their ideas into proof-of-concept (PoC) projects. It offers financial assistance to bridge the gap between ideation and commercialization.
description:
The BIG scheme is designed to: 
1. Support high-risk, innovative biotech ideas with significant commercial potential. 
2. Enable the establishment and validation of PoC for early-stage innovations. 
3. Encourage researchers to translate their research into viable products or technologies. 
4. Foster entrepreneurship among scientists and researchers by providing necessary funding and support. 

The scheme targets innovations across various biotech domains, including healthcare, agriculture, diagnostics, and industrial biotechnology.
who_can_apply:
1. Individuals: Indian citizens with innovative ideas in biotechnology. 
2. Start-ups: Early-stage companies registered in India, focusing on biotech innovations. 
3. Researchers and Academicians: Individuals from academic institutions or research organizations with promising biotech concepts. 

Applicants should not have received similar support previously and must be willing to incubate at a recognized bio-incubator if not already associated with one.
eligibility_criteria:
1. For Individuals: 
i. Must be an Indian citizen. 
ii. Should have a formal association with a recognized bio-incubator. 
iii. Should not have received similar support from other government schemes. 

2. For Start-ups: 
i. Must be a registered company in India with a focus on biotechnology. 
ii. Should be less than 5 years old at the time of application. 
iii. Annual turnover should not exceed ₹1 crore. 
iv. Should not have received BIG grant earlier. 

Detailed eligibility criteria can be found in the BIG Scheme Guidelines.
application_process: The call for proposal is announced twice a year, i.e. on 1st January and 1st July. Call for proposals typically remains open for about 45 days. The BIG Scheme is currently managed through 8 BIG Partners across the country who works with the Ignition grantees (BIG Innovators) to provide mentoring, monitoring, networking and other business development related activities.

The scheme’s mandate is to promote and encourage young students for embracing translational research to develop innovative products and technologies addressing unmet needs. SITARE-GYTI Award Grant is not a usual research fellowship. The scheme also provides an opportunity for orientation, training and mentoring through residential workshops etc.
description:
The SITARE program by BIRAC aims to foster innovation among students in biotechnology. It comprises two main components:
1. SITARE-GYTI Award Grant: Annually, 15 postgraduate or doctoral students receive up to ₹15 lakhs each to develop biotech innovations with commercial potential.
2. SITARE-Appreciation Grant: Undergraduate students participate in Biotech Innovation Ignition School (BIIS) workshops, where 10 selected participants are awarded up to ₹1 lakh each to pursue their innovative ideas.

The program includes mentorship, hands-on training, and exposure to bioincubation centers to support the entrepreneurial journey of young innovators.

name: BIRAC - SEED FUND
full_name: BIRAC SUSTAINABLE ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT FUND (SEED FUND)
about: The SEED Fund is an equity-based funding initiative by BIRAC aimed at supporting post-Proof-of-Concept (PoC) biotech startups. It provides up to ₹30 lakhs to help startups navigate the initial commercialization phase and become investment-ready.
description:
The SEED Fund is designed to bridge the critical funding gap, often referred to as the "Valley of Death," that startups face after developing a PoC but before attracting angel or venture capital investments. By offering early-stage equity support, the fund enables startups to: 
1. Advance their product development and validation processes. 
2. Establish market readiness and scalability. 
3. Attract subsequent rounds of funding from investors. 

The scheme is implemented through selected BioNEST incubators, which act as SEED Fund partners. Each partner incubator receives a grant-in-aid of ₹200 lakhs per cycle to invest in eligible startups.
eligibility_criteria:
1. Incubator should have been supported through BIRAC’s BioNEST programme.
2. Incubator should be Operational for last three years.
3. Incubator should have in-house capacity in incubating & mentoring early stage Biotech / Life Sciences Startups.
4. Incubator should have established IP&TT facilitation services for startups.
5. Incubator must have prior experience in management of early-stage funding schemes or other grants.
application_process:
To apply for the SEED Fund, startups should follow these steps: 
1. Identify a Partner Incubator: Review the list of BIRAC SEED Fund Partner BioNEST Incubators and select one that aligns with your startup's focus area.  
2. Engage with the Incubator: Reach out to the chosen incubator to understand their specific application requirements and processes. 
3. Prepare Application Materials: Develop a comprehensive proposal detailing your startup's innovation, business model, and funding needs. 
4. Submit Proposal: Submit your application through the incubator's prescribed channels, adhering to their guidelines and deadlines. 
5. Evaluation and Selection: The incubator, in collaboration with BIRAC, will evaluate the proposal based on predefined criteria and select startups for funding.

iii. Proof of concept-oriented R&D for ASICs/FPGAs

about: The ADITI scheme, part of India's strategic defense innovation initiative, offers grants up to 50% of the product development budget, with a cap of ₹25 crore, to develop critical and advanced technologies vital for national security. It aims to foster the indigenization of technologies, reduce reliance on foreign OEMs, and enhance the capabilities of the Indian defense sector through collaborative efforts involving startups, MSMEs, academia, and industry experts.
description:
ADITI (Advanced Defence Innovative Technologies Initiative) is designed to accelerate the development of critical technologies that are strategically important for India’s defense. The scheme finances up to 50% of the product development budget, encouraging projects that require substantial investment, with product development budgets around or exceeding ₹50 crore. ADITI focuses on around 30 critical technologies lacking in the current Indian ecosystem but essential for national security and with potential export capabilities. The scheme incorporates a ""Technology Watch Tool"" to align the innovation outputs with the needs of modern armed forces and supports ongoing monitoring of technological advancements.

ADITI's primary objectives include:
1. Facilitating the rapid development of innovative and sensitive defense technologies.
2. Promoting the indigenization of critical technologies to lessen dependence on foreign OEMs.
3. Enhancing products developed under the existing iDEX scheme through spiral development processes.
4. Building a Technology Watch Tool to bridge gaps between defense expectations and current capabilities.
5. Conducting technology foresight workshops to identify and refine relevant problem statements for future innovations.
6. Supporting the scale-up and integration of successfully piloted technologies into manufacturing processes.

These initiatives are crucial for building a self-reliant defense sector capable of meeting India's strategic needs and contributing to global defense markets.

2. Qualifying companies creating space-related products and services can receive funding up to Rs 1 crore.

description:
GREAT is designed to empower entrepreneurs and startups in the technical textiles field, helping them turn innovative ideas into market-ready products and technologies. The initiative offers up to INR 50 Lakhs in grant-in-aid over an 18-month period, supporting the journey from prototype to commercial product.

Benefits for Startups:
1. Financial Support: Receive up to ₹50 lakhs to help cover the costs of developing functional prototypes and commercializing new technologies.
2. Market Readiness: Accelerate the development of technical textile technologies and products to achieve market readiness.
3. Innovation Promotion: Encourages innovation in the technical textiles sector, helping startups transform creative ideas into viable solutions.
4. Ecosystem Development: Facilitates the growth of a supportive startup ecosystem within the technical textiles industry through collaboration and partnership.

This funding is pivotal for startups aiming to make significant contributions to India's self-reliance in technical textiles, providing both the capital and the framework necessary for innovation and growth.
eligibility_criteria:
i. The Startup should be incorporated as a private limited company, partnership firm, or limited liability partnership, with a turnover less than INR 100 Crores in any of the previous financial years.
ii. The Startup should be focused on innovation or improvement of existing products, services, and processes with potential for employment generation or wealth creation. Entities formed by splitting up or reconstruction of existing businesses do not qualify.
iii. The company must be registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1956/2013.
iv. The incorporation date of the company should not exceed 5 years at the time of applying for the GREAT application submission.
v. At least 51% of the capital must be owned by resident Indian citizen(s) or Indian companies that are ultimately owned and controlled by resident Indian citizen(s).
vi. The application should designate a Project Leader to represent the Startup Company.
vii. The Startup must have an adequate and functional R&D facility to execute the project, or it should be associated with or incubated at an approved incubator.

about: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals aims to enhance pharmaceutical manufacturing in India by incentivizing production and investment in high-value products such as biopharmaceuticals, complex generics, and cell-based therapies. description:
The PLI Scheme encourages pharmaceutical companies, including startups and existing firms, to scale their operations and penetrate global markets. Key aspects of the scheme include:
1. Eligible Entities: Companies, LLPs, Partnership firms, and proprietorship firms registered in India, planning to manufacture eligible products.
2. Focus Products: The scheme targets high-value pharmaceutical goods including biopharmaceuticals, patented drugs, complex generic drugs, cell-based or gene therapy drugs.
3. Financial Incentives: Incentives are based on incremental sales over a base year, with a total incentive outlay of ₹15,000 crore. The support duration is up to six years depending on meeting specified investment and sales thresholds.
4. Manufacturing Flexibility: Applicants can set up new facilities or utilize existing ones at one or more locations across India.
5. Ineligibility Criteria: Applicants with NPA status, reported as willful defaulters, or undergoing insolvency proceedings are not eligible.

This scheme is part of India’s broader "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative, aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and boosting exports. The response from the industry has been positive, with a wide range of applications received, highlighting the scheme's potential to significantly impact the pharmaceutical sector’s growth and innovation capacity.
eligibility_criteria:
1. Global Manufacturing Revenue defined as per the Scheme Guidelines for Group A (5000 crores or more), Group B (500 crore and above, upto 5000 cr) and Group C (less than 500 crore) applicants.
2. Eligibility will be subject to achievement of a minimum cumulative incremental investment over a period of five years and percentage growth in sales of manufactured goods (of Eligible Products covered under the Scheme) net of taxes (as distinct from traded goods). The cumulative investment can be made at one go, subject to annual cumulative threshold as prescribed for four years being met. An applicant is expected to meet all the minimum threshold conditions to be eligible for disbursement of incentive. The Company/ entity may invest in single or multiple eligible products to meet minimum incremental investment and sales threshold.
3. There will be a minimum investment threshold of ₹ 1000 Crores for Group A, 250 Crores for Group B and ₹ 50 Crores for Group C. Cost of land will not be counted as investment. 4. Total number of beneficiaries will be limited owing to the fixed ceiling of the budgetary outlay.

description:

5. Ongoing Opportunities: The initiative is structured to provide ongoing support through multiple funding tranches, reflecting commitment to the sustained development of selected projects.

For startups looking to engage in meaningful innovation with the potential for substantial societal impact, ANIC represents a significant opportunity to gain both financial support and valuable integration into a broader innovation ecosystem.

about: TANFUND is a funding aggregation platform sponsored by StartupTN, serving as the Tamil Nadu Government’s pivotal initiative for startup support and innovation. description:

This platform is designed to enhance the fundraising capabilities of startups by increasing their visibility within the investor community and aligning them with funding sources that match their specific growth stages and financial needs. Through TANFUND, startups gain unparalleled access to a network of venture capitalists, private equity investors, venture debt providers, family offices, and more, each offering unique advantages such as capital, expertise, and strategic networking opportunities.

Funding Partners and Their Roles
1. Venture Capitalists: Manage pooled funds to invest in startups, providing capital, business expertise, and networking opportunities.
2. Private Equity: Focuses on investing in more mature companies, often acquiring controlling interests to scale and optimize business operations.
3. Venture Debt: Offers debt financing to venture-backed startups that lack traditional collateral, often used to complement equity financing.
4. Family Offices: Invests private equity from high-net-worth families, focusing on long-term investment horizons.
5. Revenue-based Financing: Provides capital to startups in exchange for a percentage of ongoing gross revenues, with repayment terms tied to revenue performance.
6. Angel Networks: High-net-worth individuals (HNIs) who pool resources to co-invest in startups, sharing deal flow and due diligence responsibilities.
7. Government Investment Agencies: Support economic growth, innovation, employment creation, and social inclusion by funding and mentoring startups.
8. Accelerators: Offer structured programs that promote rapid startup growth through mentorship, resource access, and seed investment.

TANFUND is ideal for startups seeking strategic financial partnerships to fuel their growth and increase market presence, offering a comprehensive range of funding options tailored to meet the diverse needs of startups at various stages of their development journey.

In exchange, StartupTN acquires a 3% support stake and provides a one-year accelerator program with additional benefits.
description:
1. TANSEED 7.0, an initiative under StartupTN, operates as a Support Equity-linked grant fund, offering significant financial assistance to propel the growth of startups within Tamil Nadu.
2. The fund specifically targets startups that are developing innovative products or cutting-edge technologies, distinguishing them from businesses primarily focused on service delivery.

4. This accelerator provides crucial mentorship from experienced professionals, valuable networking opportunities within the startup ecosystem, and facilitated participation in both national and international delegations.

6. By combining financial backing with intensive guidance and exposure, this initiative plays a vital role in fostering a robust and innovative startup landscape within Tamil Nadu.
eligibility_criteria:
1. Entity Type: Must be registered as a Private Limited Company under the Companies Act 2013. Applications from entities currently registered as LLPs or Partnerships will also be considered if they are willing to convert to a Private Limited Company.
2. Startup Registration: Should be registered with TANSIM and STARTUP INDIA and located in Tamil Nadu.
3. Financial Criteria: The average profit per the income tax return for the last three years (or lesser if newly registered) should be less than Rs. 5 Lakhs.
4. Innovation Requirement: Must be working towards innovation, development, or improvement of products or processes that have a high potential for employment generation, social impact, or wealth creation. Startups must have at least a Proof of Concept (PoC) or a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) and use technology in its core product, service, or business model.
5. Company History: The entity should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstruction of a business already in existence or as a subsidiary, joint venture, or associate of another company.
6. Legal Standing: Should have cleared all dues with Government agencies and not be blacklisted by any Government agency in India.
7. Incubation: The applicant may need to be incubated for at least six months at the time of application.
8. Ownership: Should be an Indian startup with at least 51% shareholding by Indian promoters. OCI and PIO holders are considered Indian citizens for this scheme.
9. Sector Restrictions: The Seed Fund is generally not available for service companies operating in traditional trade and commerce.
10. Funding Usage: The fund is intended for the development of a prototype, a market-ready product, or small-level pilot production, and not for regular research activities typical of universities or colleges.

description:
1. A Key Partner for the IT Sector: For businesses operating within the Information Technology (IT) domain, the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) serves as a significant ally in fostering growth and development.
2. Comprehensive Ecosystem Support: STPI provides a range of crucial benefits, including tax advantages, robust infrastructure support, and well-equipped incubation facilities, all aimed at nurturing the expansion of IT and IT-enabled Services (ITES) units.
3. Significant Reach and Export Contribution: The scheme has supported a substantial network of over 85,000 STPI units, which have collectively generated impressive exports valued at over Rs. 5.5 lakh crore, highlighting the scheme's substantial contribution to the Indian technology sector.
4. Financial and Infrastructural Advantages: The benefits offered include exemptions on profits and import duties, along with the provision of essential infrastructure within designated STPI centers across the country.
5. Targeting Export-Oriented Tech Businesses: The eligibility criteria for STPI support primarily focus on IT and ITES companies that have a clear intention and focus on exporting their services and products.
6. Focus on Future Technologies: Recognizing the evolving landscape of the tech industry, STPI has launched special initiatives like "STPI NEXT," which specifically targets and supports companies working in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality (AR/VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT).
who_can_apply:

2. Entities: Including private limited companies, partnership firms, and LLPs.

eligibility_criteria:
1. Company Age: Incorporated within the last 10 years.
2. Annual Turnover: Not exceeding ₹100 crore in any financial year since incorporation.
3. Original Entity: Should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business.
4. Innovation: Working towards innovation, development, or improvement of products, processes, or services, or having a scalable business model with high potential for employment generation or wealth creation.
application_process: Interested applicants can apply online through the STPI Startup Portal by selecting the relevant program (e.g., LEAP, NGIS, CoEs) and submitting the required documentation as per the specific program guidelines.

name: Ebiz Portal
about: Ebiz is a single-window platform that simplifies business registrations and approvals, processing over 1.3 crore registrations. It offers services like company registration, GST compliance, and licenses, with benefits including faster processing and online tracking.
description:
1. A Unified Solution for Regulatory Hurdles: For entrepreneurs facing the complexities of registrations and approvals, Ebiz serves as a comprehensive, single-window platform designed to streamline these often-cumbersome processes.
2. Significant Time and Effort Savings: By consolidating various regulatory requirements into one platform, Ebiz demonstrably saves valuable time and effort for entrepreneurs seeking to establish and operate their businesses.
3. Proven Efficiency in Processing Registrations: The platform's effectiveness is highlighted by the impressive processing of over 1.3 crore registrations, showcasing its capacity to simplify business operations on a large scale.
4. Comprehensive Suite of Essential Services: Ebiz offers a wide array of crucial services, including company registration, Goods and Services Tax (GST) compliance, and assistance with obtaining various necessary licenses, approvals, and clearances.
5. Key Advantages for Businesses: Utilizing Ebiz provides businesses with the benefits of faster processing times for regulatory requirements, a convenient single point of access for all necessary procedures, and the ability to track the progress of their applications online.
6. Mobile Accessibility for Convenience: Recognizing the need for flexibility, Ebiz also offers a Mobile App, providing entrepreneurs with the convenience of accessing the platform's resources and services on the go.
who_can_apply: Entrepreneurs, businesses, and investors seeking to obtain various government-to-business (G2B) services, including approvals, registrations, and licenses, can apply through the eBiz portal.
eligibility_criteria:
Eligibility varies based on the specific service:
1. Industrial License (IL): Required for industries under compulsory licensing.

full_name: Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund

about: The Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF) provides financial assistance with an outlay of Rs. 10,861 crore to set up or expand dairy processing units. It supports modernization, capacity building, and infrastructure development, benefiting over 5 lakh milk producers.
description:
1. Financial Support for Dairy Sector Expansion: DIDF provides financial assistance to establish new or expand existing milk processing units, with a significant financial commitment of Rs. 10,861 crore.
2. Empowering Milk Producers for Inclusive Growth: The program aims to benefit over 5 lakh milk producers, fostering inclusive growth and development within the dairy sector.
3. Comprehensive Support for Infrastructure Development: DIDF offers grant-in-aid for various crucial aspects, including the modernization of existing processing units, the establishment of new units, and initiatives focused on capacity building within the dairy industry.
4. Wide Range of Eligible Beneficiaries: Dairy cooperatives, farmer-producer organizations (FPOs), and private companies operating in the dairy sector are eligible to receive support under this fund.
5. Focus on Strengthening Dairy Infrastructure: The financial assistance provided is specifically targeted towards the development of essential infrastructure, the acquisition of modern processing equipment, and the establishment of efficient cold chain facilities to improve the overall dairy ecosystem.
who_can_apply:
Eligible applicants include:

name: SIPPS
application_open: The scheme is open for applications from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026.
about: The Startup Intellectual Property Protection Scheme (SIPPS) reimburses 50% of IP filing fees (up to Rs. 5 lakh) for patents, trademarks, and copyrights, supporting registered startups in protecting their innovations and intellectual property rights.
description:
1. Supporting Intellectual Property Protection for Startups: Recognizing the importance of safeguarding innovative ideas, the Scheme for Intellectual Property Protection for Startups (SIPPS) offers financial reimbursement to startups for the costs associated with filing patents, trademarks, and copyrights.
2. Significant Reimbursement for IP Filing Costs: SIPPS reimburses startups for 50% of their filing fees for patents, trademarks, and copyrights, with a maximum reimbursement limit of Rs. 5 lakh.
3. Targeting Registered Startups Meeting Criteria: The eligibility for this reimbursement is specifically for registered startups that meet certain defined criteria, ensuring the benefit reaches legitimate new ventures.
4. Encouraging Innovation and Brand Protection: The primary benefits of SIPPS are to actively encourage startups to pursue innovation and to provide them with the means to legally protect their valuable intellectual property rights, thereby empowering them to build their brand with confidence and security.
who_can_apply:
1. Recognized Startups: Entities recognized by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Startup India initiative.
2. Indian Innovators/Creators: Individuals filing IP applications through Technology and Innovation Support Centers (TISCs) in India.
3. Educational Institutes: Indian educational institutions meeting specific criteria outlined in the scheme.
4. Applicants Filing International Patents: Indian applicants filing international patent applications through Receiving Office, India (RO/IN) or International Bureau, WIPO (RO/IB), electing India as International Search Authority (ISA).
eligibility_criteria:
Applicants must:
1. Be a DPIIT-recognized startup, Indian innovator/creator, or eligible educational institution.
2. Submit a self-declaration stating they have not availed funds under any other government scheme for paying facilitator fees.
3. Engage an empanelled facilitator for filing and prosecuting their IP applications.

description:
1. Facilitating Global Market Entry: The Market Access Initiatives (MAPS) program is designed to help businesses realize their international ambitions by providing financial assistance for participation in key global trade events.
2. Opening Doors to International Opportunities: By supporting participation in international trade fairs, exhibitions, and buyer-seller meets, MAPS effectively opens doors for Indian companies to access new markets and explore diverse opportunities for growth.
3. Significant Impact on Export Performance: The program has demonstrated its effectiveness in propelling global ambitions, having benefited over 8,000 companies and contributed to the generation of exports exceeding Rs. 28,000 crore.
4. Financial Assistance for International Market Engagement: MAPS offers crucial financial support specifically for companies to participate in international trade fairs, exhibitions, and buyer-seller meetings, reducing the financial barrier to global market entry.
5. Targeting Export-Oriented Businesses: Eligibility for the program is primarily for export-oriented companies that are registered with the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).
6. Connecting Businesses with Global Buyers: A key benefit of MAPS is its ability to connect Indian businesses directly with potential international buyers, thereby significantly increasing their export opportunities and facilitating global partnerships.

name: CMEGP
application_open: Applications are accepted year-round through the CMEGP e-portal.
reservation: Women , SC/ST , Backward Class , Minority , Differently Abled , Youth
about: The Chief Minister Employment Generation Programme (CMEGP) is a state-sponsored credit-linked subsidy scheme aimed at promoting self-employment by supporting new micro and small enterprises in Maharashtra. It provides financial assistance, technical support, and training to young entrepreneurs, with a focus on rural and urban areas.
description:
1. CMEGP targets the establishment of new micro and small enterprises in manufacturing, service, agro-based, and primary agro-processing sectors.
2. The scheme offers financial assistance in the form of term loans and subsidies, with a maximum project cost of ₹50 lakh.
3. Special provisions are made for women, SC/ST, OBC, ex-servicemen, and differently-abled individuals, including higher subsidy rates and relaxed age criteria.
4. The program emphasizes skill development through Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) and supports entities like SHGs, proprietorships, partnerships, and LLPs.
5. Implementation is carried out through the Directorate of Industries (DOI), District Industries Centers (DICs), and Maharashtra State Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs).
who_can_apply:
1. Individuals aged between 18 and 45 years.
2. For special categories (SC/ST/OBC/Women/Ex-servicemen/Differently-abled), the age limit is relaxed by 5 years.
3. Applicants must be residents of Maharashtra or possess a domicile certificate.
4. Only one person per family is eligible for assistance.
5. Eligible entities include proprietorships, partnerships, Self-Help Groups (SHGs), One Person Companies (OPCs), and Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs).
eligibility_criteria:
1. Minimum educational qualification: 7th standard pass for projects costing above ₹10 lakh; 10th standard pass for projects above ₹25 lakh.
2. Only new projects are eligible; existing units or those that have availed benefits under other government schemes are not eligible.
3. The project cost should not include the cost of land; however, ready-built work sheds/workshops are admissible up to 20% of the total project cost.
4. Working capital is limited to 30% of the total project cost.
5. Applicants must provide necessary documents such as Aadhaar card, educational certificates, domicile certificate, and project report.
application_process:
1. Register on the CMEGP e-portal.
2. Fill in the online application form with personal and project details.
3. Upload required documents (Aadhaar, educational certificates, project report).
4. Submit the application for review by the implementing agency.
5. Upon approval, undergo Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training.
thrust_areas:
1. Promotion of new micro and small enterprises in rural and urban areas.
2. Support for manufacturing, service, agro-based, and primary agro-processing sectors.
3. Encouragement of entrepreneurship among women, SC/ST, OBC, ex-servicemen, and differently-abled individuals.
4. Development of infrastructure such as work sheds and workshops.

about: The PMEGP is a credit-linked subsidy scheme under Ministry of MSME, Government of India, implemented through KVIC, State Khadi & Village Industries Boards (KVIB), and DICs, aimed at generating self-employment opportunities by supporting micro enterprises in the non-farm sector.
description:
1. PMEGP provides financial assistance (subsidised loans) for setting up new micro units in manufacturing, service, and business sectors, both in rural and urban areas. 
2. The scheme offers different subsidy rates depending on whether the applicant belongs to general category or special categories (SC/ST, women etc.), and also the rural or urban location. 
3. It aims to support both small new projects and upgrading/expansion of existing eligible units. 
4. The scheme mandates some minimum qualification (VIII standard pass) for projects above certain cost thresholds in both manufacturing and service sectors. 
5. Support is given for micro-enterprises in non-farm activities, excluding certain prohibited / negative-list activities.
who_can_apply:
1. Any individual aged 18 years or above. 
2. Through implementing agencies: KVIC, State KVIB / Board, or District Industries Centre (DIC).
eligibility_criteria:
1. Must be 18+ years old. 
2. No income ceiling for new project assistance. 
3. For projects costing > ₹10 lakh in manufacturing and > ₹5 lakh in service/business sector, beneficiary must be at least VIII standard pass. 
4. Only new projects sanctioned under PMEGP are eligible (i.e. not existing enterprises except in specific cases of upgradation where allowed). 
5. Only one person per family (self + spouse) can get assistance under PMEGP.
application_process:
1. Visit PMEGP portal (KVIC online) and register application. 
2. Fill in required forms with project details (cost, sector, operations) via portal. 
3. Submit eligibility documents (age proof, education certificate if needed, bank account, identity etc.). 
4. Application goes through appraisal via DIC/KVIC / KVIB for sanction, checking viability. 
5. After sanction, beneficiary may have to undergo EDP (Entrepreneurship Development Programme) training (online or offline) before final disbursement.
thrust_areas:
1. Promote self-employment via micro enterprises in manufacturing and services/business sectors. 
2. Facilitate artisan / village industry development, especially through KVIC / KVIB etc. 
3. Encourage projects in rural as well as urban areas, with special subsidy support for certain categories (SC/ST, women, special areas). 
4. Support for upgrading/expansion of existing micro-units under certain conditions.

name: TNYIEDP
full_name: Tamil Nadu Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development Programme
about: The Tamil Nadu Youth Innovation & Entrepreneurship Development Programme (TNYIEDP, also known as “Nimirnthu Nil”) is an initiative by the Government of Tamil Nadu / EDII-TN to promote student entrepreneurship in higher educational institutions. It aims to identify and nurture young innovators, provide training, mentorship, and support to convert ideas into startups.
description:
1. Focuses on students in colleges (engineering, polytechnic, arts & science, agriculture, medical) to foster an entrepreneurial mindset. 
2. Emphasis on innovation, ideation, bootcamps and specialised training (for example in AI, e-commerce, manufacturing) to build skills relevant for startups. 
3. Support includes institutional “hubs” (district hubs) where colleges coordinate, and administration is involved to facilitate idea generation and startup support. 
4. Financial backing for top ideas (cash prizes etc.), resources for idea development, and facilitating linkages (mentors, ecosystem) for early stage students. 
5. A goal to reach a large number of student entrepreneurs over time (e.g. in one instance, targeting 10,000 student entrepreneurs with allocated funds) to scale the entrepreneurial culture.
who_can_apply:
1. College/university students of higher education institutions in Tamil Nadu.
2. Institutional participation via colleges (engineering, polytechnic, arts & science, agriculture, medical) through their college administrations.
eligibility_criteria:
1. Must be a student (in higher education) in one of the participating colleges. 
2. The idea / startup proposal should be at ideation or early venture stage (not specified in detail, but implied since it is for student entrepreneurs).
3. Likely restrictions like first time idea, possibly no existing business scale – but not clearly documented.
application_process:
1. Colleges (or students) are mobilized to participate under their district hub under EDII-TN. 
2. Students submit idea proposals via their institution or EDII hub.
3. Ideas may go through bootcamps / ideation & innovation training sessions.
4. Top ideas are selected for further support, mentoring, and possible cash prize.
5. Implementation or further incubation for promising ideas aided by EDII or partnering institutions.
thrust_areas:
1. Student entrepreneurship & ideation in higher education institutions.
2. Specialized training in emerging technologies (AI, e-commerce, manufacturing). 
3. Institutional hubs / bootcamps / mentoring & innovation ecosystem building.
4. Recognition & rewards (cash prizes) for top startup ideas to motivate participation.
